items.briefing:
Home batteries and solar systems connected to the internet are now flagged as a cybersecurity compliance concern for Australian organisations — if staff use these at home while working remotely, they could inadvertently expose work systems to risk. Separately, Asia Pacific leaders are calling for stronger defences against scams, reflecting the ongoing threat to Australians from fraud and social engineering attacks targeting both individuals and workplaces.

AI tools are also creating new security challenges, with traditional security controls struggling to keep pace with automated AI systems acting on behalf of users. Be cautious about which AI tools you connect to work accounts.

**Tip:** Only connect approved AI tools to your work systems — check with your IT team before linking any new app or service.

featured.title: Australia's home batteries are now a cybersecurity compliance isue
featured.summary: Millions of rooftop batteries are now subject to mandatory cyber standards as Canberra widens scrutiny of grid-connected home devices.
